cls: Antineoplastic - oral selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD)
pharm: Oral SERD that binds estrogen receptor alpha and triggers its degradation; active against ESR1-mutant tumours resistant to aromatase inhibitors
quick: With food (reduces nausea; take at the same time daily).
Can cause fetal harm; verify status; effective contraception during and after treatment per labeling
Do not breastfeed during treatment and after last dose per labeling
See full labeling; monitor renal function with diarrhoea/vomiting/dehydration risk
See full labeling; dose-reduce in moderate-severe impairment for hepatically cleared agents
No specific interaction; avoid excess with hepatotoxic or myelosuppressive therapy
CBC, LFTs, drug-specific toxicities, pregnancy status
summary: Elacestrant (Orserdu) is the first oral SERD, indicated for ER-positive HER2-negative ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer after at least one line of endocrine therapy. Benefit concentrates in ESR1-mutant disease (EMERALD), so mutation testing is required. Notable toxicities are hypertriglyceridaemia/hypercholesterolaemia, nausea, musculoskeletal pain and embryo-fetal risk.
indications: ER-positive HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression after at least one line of endocrine therapy

dosage.d: 345 mg once daily continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.t: Take with food at the same time daily; swallow whole
dosage.n: Reduce to 258 mg daily for grade 3+ toxicity or with moderate hepatic impairment; avoid in severe impairment

admin: Take exactly as prescribed; do not crush, split or chew unless labeling allows
Take at the same time(s) each day; if a dose is missed follow the missed-dose rule - do not double
Report interacting new medicines including antifungals, anti-TB drugs, antiepileptics and St John's wort (CYP3A4)
Store in the original container with desiccant where supplied; protect from moisture
moa: Elacestrant is an oral selective estrogen receptor degrader: it binds estrogen receptor alpha, blocks its signalling and marks it for proteasomal degradation, retaining activity against constitutively active ESR1-mutant receptors that resist aromatase inhibitors.
preg: No adequate human data. Based on mechanism, fetal harm is expected. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose. Use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Because of potential serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose.
renal: Mild-moderate impairment: no routine change unless labeled; severe: limited data - monitor for exaggerated toxicity and dehydration-related AKI.
hepatic: Mild impairment: monitor; moderate-severe: dose-reduce or avoid per labeling (most agents hepatically cleared).

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (raise exposure - avoid per labeling caution)
moderate: P-gp and BCRP substrates (elacestrant may alter exposure)
interactions.food: With food (reduces nausea; take at the same time daily).
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excess alcohol with hepatotoxic therapy.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

emergency: Severe vomiting preventing fluids/medicines - seek urgent care
Chest pain or pancreatitis-type pain with very high triglycerides - seek emergency care

counsel: Take with food at the same time each day; tell the team if nausea prevents eating
You need an ESR1 mutation blood/tumour test for this drug to be appropriate
Report muscle/bone pain, unusual fatigue or abdominal pain
Avoid new antifungal, TB or seizure medicines without checking (interactions); use contraception
pk: Target inhibition within hours-days; response assessed in weeks
Room temperature 20-25 C in original container; protect from moisture
pearls: First oral SERD - degrades ER rather than just blocking it, overcoming ESR1-mutant resistance
Test for ESR1 mutation: wild-type benefit is minimal
Lipid rises are a class-distinctive monitoring item versus injectable fulvestrant
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day unless it is near the next dose; never double up. Take as soon as remembered on the same day; do not double.
overdose: No specific antidote. Withhold drug and give supportive care with monitoring of CBC, ECG, LFTs and agent-specific toxicities. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
